# QnALog 1.7.7

Name corrections from the glossary and from a note's errata now reach imported notes, regenerated notes and their titles.

## Fixed

- **Imported audio now uses the glossary's corrections.** When audio was imported as a whole file (Alibaba Cloud file transcription or OpenRouter speaker separation), the transcript skipped the glossary's "misspelling => correct" entries, so a misheard name stayed wrong even though the glossary listed the fix. Imported transcripts now get the same corrections as recordings.
- **Reorganizing applies the glossary to older notes.** Reorganize, Save as new version and Clean transcript now apply the glossary's corrections together with the note's own errata. A note transcribed before you added a glossary entry gets the corrected spelling when you reorganize it. When the glossary and the note's errata list the same misspelling, the note's errata wins. The raw transcript keeps the original text.
- **Save as new version corrects the file name and properties.** A name fixed in the note's errata is now also corrected in the new version's file name, heading and properties copied from the original (such as people and tags). The original note, its file name and the recording path are not changed.
- **Task panel spinner.** The spinner next to a running queued task (for example a transcription retry) is round again instead of a squashed ellipse.

## User impact

- The settings schema version is unchanged. No settings are dropped or changed by the upgrade.
- No need to reconfigure services or API keys.
- Existing notes are not rewritten by the upgrade. Corrections apply the next time you import, reorganize or save a new version.
- A version file generated before 1.7.7 keeps its old, wrong file name. Saving a new version writes a file with the corrected name; delete the old one if you no longer need it.
- Reorganize in place still does not rename a note that already has a title.

## Known issue

- A task ticked in a note still returns to unticked after **Reorganize** or after switching to another saved version of that note. The earlier version is kept in the note's version history.
